newsitem.title: UK: DLR FINDS SUPPORT AFTER HAWKISH BUBA BOOSTS MARK.
newsitem.headline: DLR FINDS SUPPORT AFTER HAWKISH BUBA BOOSTS MARK.

text.p: The dollar hovered just above session lows against the mark on Wednesday after the German unit rose across the board, boosted by a hawkish assessment on German inflation by the Bundesbank, traders said.

In its August monthly report the Bundesbank said it could not be overlooked that there had been a stronger rise in consumer prices in recent months and it would orientate its policy so that price stability could be maintained.
Forex traders took this as an indication that the Bundesbank might be preparing the ground for higher German rates, and they bought marks against the dollar and on the European crosses.

"There has been a general move into marks this morning after the Bundesbank report," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN AMRO in London. "The report showed that the Bundesbank is concerned about inflation and that has increased speculation about a German rate rise."
The dollar gradually shed about a pfennig in the wake of the Bundesbank's report but found strong support just below 1.85 marks.
At 1137 GMT the dollar was at 1.8504/14 marks, up from a session low of 1.8480 but down from 1.8638/48 in late European trading on Tuesday.
Against the yen it hovered at 116.40/50 from 116.75.

The Bundesbank also said it will observe further currency rate movements closely with a view to the risks presented for price stability. The comment follows on the heels of recent concern voiced by Bundesbankers about the weakness of the mark.

"The assertion that the exchange rate is very significant in policy decisions, the fact they highlight the recent rise in some inflation figures and the desire to see M3 growth lower suggest that they may be closer to a rate increase than previously thought," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.
German consumer price inflation quickened to 1.9 percent in July, the highest level since June 1995 and up from 1.7 in June.

Though the CPI was boosted by one-off factors last month, economists expect it to rise above 2.0 percent soon, the level regarded as acceptable by the Bundesbank. Germany's import prices, due later this month, are also key for signs of whether the mark's weakness is boosting inflation.

A robust rise of 2.0 percent in real term June retail sales also helped to underpin mark gains, dealers said. However, the data series is erratic and in the first six months of 1997, retail sales were down one percent.
The immediate focus is now on US retail sales and producer price data for July, due at 1230 GMT.

Dollar/yen's movements were closely linked to the mark/yen cross, which pushed through firm resistance at 62.60/70 overnight on short-covering and stop-loss buying but baulked just above 63 yen in European trading.
The yen is likely to stay soft amid concern about Japan's economy, analysts said.
Eisuke Sakakibara, Japan's vice-minister for international affairs, is scheduled to meet U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers in Washington on Wednesday.
Mark/yen was at 62.96/99, up from 62.24/27 at the close here on Tuesday. The mark has recovered from two-year lows just above 62 yen on Monday.

Sterling was weighed down by a stronger mark, traders said. It showed little net response to the Bank of England's quarterly inflation report and to better-than-expected UK jobs data for July and flat June average earnings figures.
The pound was at 2.9115/25, down from 2.9399/9404 in late trade on Tuesday. Against the dollar it stood at $1.5743/53 from $1.5770/80. -- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
